notes.n9.assistant: Concentrated: ChatGPT leads globally; Gemini, Meta AI and Copilot ride platform distribution; China has a separate field (Doubao, Qwen, Yuanbao, DeepSeek, Kimi).
notes.n9.coding: Hottest app category of 2025-26: Cursor sold to SpaceX for $60B (closed Aug 2026) and Cognition valued at $48B (Sep 2026); model labs (Claude Code, Codex) compete directly.
notes.n9.agentic: Browser and computer-use agents consolidating into big platforms: Meta bought Manus, Atlassian bought Dia, Anthropic bought Vercept, OpenAI shipped Atlas.
notes.n9.knowledge: Suite vendors (Microsoft, Google, Atlassian) bundle work AI; Glean is the leading independent; meeting notetakers are a crowded sub-niche.
notes.n9.support: Sierra (>$15B, May 2026) and Decagon lead AI-native players; incumbents Salesforce, Zendesk and Intercom ship their own agents.
notes.n9.voice: India has a dense cluster of Indic-language voice-agent startups (Bolna, Ringg, Navana, Nurix, Smallest.ai, Gnani, Sarvam) competing on language coverage and per-minute cost.
notes.n9.gtm: Clay ($7.1B, 2026) leads GTM data/agents; AI-SDR startups face churn questions while CRM incumbents add agents.
notes.n9.creative: Incumbent design suites (Canva, Adobe, Figma) vs generative-native media apps; Chinese video models (Kling) competitive globally.
notes.n9.legal: Two-horse race at the top: Harvey (~$15.5B) and Legora ($8.8B, Oct 2026), both acquiring; legal publishers (TR, LexisNexis) defend with content.
notes.n9.health: Ambient scribes the fastest-adopted category (Abridge, Microsoft Dragon, Ambience); clinical search (OpenEvidence) and imaging AI mature.
notes.n9.finance: Research copilots (AlphaSense, Rogo, Hebbia) for investors; separate wave of AI-native accounting/ERP (Basis, Rillet, Campfire).
notes.n9.hr: HCM incumbents consolidating AI recruiting (Workday bought Paradox and Sana in 2025); Mercor pivoted to expert supply for AI labs.
notes.n9.secops: Platform vendors embed agents; dozens of AI-SOC startups (Dropzone, 7AI, Prophet, Exaforce) and AI pentesters (XBOW, Horizon3) compete.
notes.n9.edu: Consumer learning apps and homework helpers dominate usage; Chinese/ByteDance homework apps large globally.
notes.n9.industrial: AI drug discovery best funded; new 'AI scientist' labs (Lila, Periodic) and engineering-simulation AI (PhysicsX, Neural Concept).
notes.n9.physical: Robotaxis commercial (Waymo, Baidu, Pony, WeRide); humanoids capital-intensive and China-heavy, with Unitree's Aug 2026 Shanghai IPO the first major listing.
notes.n9.consumer: Companion apps under safety and monetisation pressure: Character.AI filed Chapter 11 in Oct 2026.
notes.n9.devices: Smart glasses (Meta-EssilorLuxottica) are the breakout form factor; early pins/pendants failed or were acquired (Humane, Limitless, Bee).
notes.n9.store: Distribution shifting to in-assistant app directories (ChatGPT, Claude) and cloud marketplaces selling agents to enterprises.
notes.n9.public: Defence AI is the most heavily funded vertical in 2026 (Anduril, Helsing, Shield AI); sovereign LLM vendors (Mistral, Cohere) win government frameworks.
notes.n9.commerce: Platforms own the agent (Amazon, OpenAI, Google, Perplexity) and protocols (ACP, AP2/UCP); retailers and search vendors adapt catalogues for agent buyers.
notes.n9.itops: ServiceNow consolidated the category by buying Moveworks (Dec 2025); remaining independents compete inside Teams/Slack.
notes.n9.analytics: Warehouse vendors (Snowflake, Databricks) and BI incumbents embed agents; AI-native analysts (Hex, Julius) target business users.
notes.n9.lang: MT is commoditising via frontier LLMs; DeepL leads specialist MT, LSPs (RWS, TransPerfect) shift to AI-first, and dubbing moves to voice-AI vendors.
notes.n9.insurance: Insurance AI is maturing via acquisitions (Applied-Cytora); real estate led by EliseAI ($4B); construction AI centred on site capture and document agents.
notes.n9.supply: Planning suites (o9, Kinaxis, Blue Yonder) add agents; agentic procurement (Pactum, Zip) and agri robotics are the growth niches.
notes.n9.sor: Incumbent systems of record (Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP, Workday) are adding agent layers, while AI-native challengers rebuild the record itself around a knowledge graph.
